title: Workflow workspace and registration records (DEL-02-02 WR-v0.2) - PROPOSED
description: The formats the workflow workspace hands to its receivers (WORKSPACE_AND_REGISTRATION.md section 8; v0.2 adds C-02's two elements, the L-4 multi-entry A15 descriptor and shipped-revision standing, and the R19-7 run text and supply check; CC-WR-RECONFIRM, in place, adds the DS-8 re-confirmation of a registered revision to registration_disposition, draft_transition, a15_descriptor and library_entry). PROPOSED (R17-1); Chirality names only, snake_case as WD's schema; no supplier wire field. Every record names its kind in record_kind. Workflow identities are WD's tuple, referenced by WD's $id (workflow-declaration.schema.json#/$defs/workflow_identity); RS spells the same tuple in camelCase (RS $defs/workflowTuple). Keywords are kept to the subset that DEL-04-03's design validator (prototype/minischema.py) checks, which has no maxLength, so the name's length bound is written as a pattern lookahead. Rules a schema cannot state (for example that an A15 descriptor's subject revision equals its bound content value) are reader checks, listed in WR section 8.

name.description: Package name (WD section 7: 1-64 lowercase letters or digits in hyphen-separated segments; folder name equals name).

content_identity.description: A content identity with its method designation. For a draft it is computed over the draft folder by WD section 6.1 RV-1...RV-5; for a revision it is the revision value. The algorithm is open (WD U-03); the prototype's proto-sha256-list-0 is an illustration.

identity.description: WD section 6.1 tuple, by reference to WD's schema.

revision_identity.description: A tuple that names selected content: revision required (WD section 6.1: without revision a tuple names a slot).

slot.description: A library slot: origin, source root and name, no revision (WD section 6.1).

draft_key.description: Where a draft is. A draft has no workflow identity (EXEC TR-1, HR-3); it is named by its location and folder name, and its content by a content identity.

enum: shipped revision held in this library

draft_reference.description: WR section 2.3 and 5.1. Supplied to DEL-01-04's draft receiving interface (DEP-01-04-009) and cited by the A15 descriptor and the library entry.

allOf.description: The name follows WD's rule unless the draft is reported not valid (HY-2).
A base is recorded only by the App (WR SP-3).

draft_transition.description: WR section 5.1 event, supplied to DEL-01-04 (DEP-01-04-009: draft/registration/collision/refusal transitions for native presentation).

attribution.description: Who changed the files, where observed: a supplier fileChange item naming the path (observed-in-generated-types at 0.158.0), an App action, or not observed (a shell write or the person's editor).

a15_record.description: C-02 (R18-1): the RS human_act A15 record the App act control wrote; on 'registered', 'registration not completed' and (CC-WR-RECONFIRM) 're-confirmed' only.

revision.description: C-02 (R18-1): the registered revision identity; on 'registered' and (CC-WR-RECONFIRM) on 're-confirmed', where it is the re-confirmed revision's own identity, not a new one.

allOf.description: C-02: a15_record only on 'registered' or 'registration not completed'; CC-WR-RECONFIRM adds 're-confirmed'.
C-02: revision only on 'registered'; CC-WR-RECONFIRM adds 're-confirmed'.

CC-WR-RECONFIRM: a 're-confirmed' event ends in 'registered, unchanged since' with disposition 're-confirmation', and names the content, the A15 record and the re-confirmed revision (NIR's draft-transition rule, mirrored).
CC-WR-RECONFIRM: a 'registered' event never carries the re-confirmation disposition.

reconfirmed_revision.description: CC-WR-RECONFIRM (WR section 4.8 RC-3, RC-4, RC-9): the registered revision a re-confirmation names: its full tuple exactly as its registered ledger line records it, and that line's ledger_seq and sequence. A re-confirmation registers no new revision.

registration_disposition.description: WR section 4.1 DS-1...DS-7: the registration collision and disposition report, shown in the review and supplied to DEL-01-04. A discovery collision (C-1) uses the same entries list with disposition absent.

reconfirms.description: CC-WR-RECONFIRM: DS-8 only, the registered revision the review offers to re-confirm (WR section 4.8 RC-1). prior_revision keeps its meaning for every review: the slot's latest revision at review (WR section 4.8 RC-4).

allOf.description: CC-WR-RECONFIRM: DS-8 (re-confirmation) names the registered revision it re-confirms; no other disposition does.
A registration review states a disposition and the reviewed content; a discovery report does not.
DS-2: a new revision names the prior revision; DS-1: a new workflow has none.

a15_descriptor.description: WR section 4.3 RB-4: what the workspace hands DEL-01-04's act control to present and capture A15 (K-8). Bound content equals the subject's revision (reader check). Relations named per R17-11: the reviewed draft content and the prior revision; derived_from is WD's parent-identity relation. CC-WR-RECONFIRM (WR section 4.8 RC-4): for DS-8 the descriptor re-confirms a registered revision: disposition 're-confirmation', its own wording and purpose, subject equal to reconfirms.identity (reader check), prior_revision and derived_from as that revision's registered line records them; no new revision is registered.

reconfirms.description: CC-WR-RECONFIRM: DS-8 only, the registered revision this act re-confirms (WR section 4.8 RC-4).

freshness.description: RB-3: the descriptor is current only while the live draft still has this content and the slot's latest revision is still prior_revision (or the slot is still empty). CC-WR-RECONFIRM (WR section 4.8 RC-5): for a re-confirmation descriptor (disposition 're-confirmation') the slot's latest revision is compared with slot_latest, the slot's latest at review, because relations.prior_revision is then the re-confirmed revision's own prior.

allOf.description: CC-WR-RECONFIRM: a re-confirmation descriptor (disposition 're-confirmation') carries the re-confirm wording and purpose and names the revision it re-confirms; any other descriptor keeps the registration wording and purpose and names none.

enum: make it available again in this App session from the project library
make it available again in this App session from the user library
make it available in the project library
make it available in the user library

library_entry.description: WR section 4.6 and 6 SQ-G: one line of a library's registration ledger (App-kept, R17-4). 'registered' is the commit point of a registration; 'not completed' records an A15 whose registration did not complete. Registered standing also needs the cited A15 record and store bytes that recompute (LS-1). CC-WR-RECONFIRM (WR section 4.8): 're-confirmed' is the commit point of a re-confirmation (G-4R): it cites the new A15 and, in reconfirms, the earlier 'registered' line of the same revision; it adds no revision to the slot's series and never changes the slot's latest (reader checks RC-9). A 'not completed' line with disposition 're-confirmation' records a re-confirmation that did not complete.

disposition.description: 'in place' covers single and multi-entry in-place registrations (DS-7, §4.7). 're-confirmation' (CC-WR-RECONFIRM, DS-8) is carried by 're-confirmed' lines and by 'not completed' lines of a re-confirmation.

reviewed_entry.description: L-4: for an in-place registration of a library entry reviewed directly (WR §4.7), the entry's ID-3 string and content.

reconfirms.description: CC-WR-RECONFIRM: on a re-confirmation line only, the earlier 'registered' line this line re-confirms (WR section 4.8 RC-9).

allOf.description: CC-WR-RECONFIRM: a line names the revision it re-confirms exactly when its disposition is 're-confirmation'.
CC-WR-RECONFIRM: a re-confirmation is of a reviewed draft (WR section 4.8 RC-1), never of an entry reviewed in place.
Exactly one of reviewed_draft and reviewed_entry.

selection_record.description: WR section 4.4 SL-1...SL-6: the person's explicit selection of registered content, handed to DEL-02-03 (CK-1, A-1; the resolver) and DEL-04-03 (R2 selected link). DEL-02-04 receives no selection: it composes role guidance only (R19-7, which dropped R17-8's workflow supply).

prior_run.description: R19-2 (a)/(b): the run that came before in this conversation; a relation, not part of the identity.

ended.description: How the earlier run ended; RX2 (R20-11 (4)) adds 'ended to start <B>' for the one-step End A and start B without a finished report.

proposal.description: R19-2 (b): the agent message whose proposal line the person confirmed; never a selection by itself.

proposed_name.description: RX (R20-5, R20-9): the proposal line's '<origin>:<name>', exactly as the agent wrote it.

allOf.description: A confirmed agent proposal cites the proposal; other selections do not.

how.const: agent proposal confirmed by the person

trial_pointer.description: WR section 4.2 TT-4 (K-7): an App-kept pointer that the person tried a draft in an ordinary conversation. It names draft content, never a workflow identity, and is not a run record, compatibility evidence or A15 evidence.

standing.const: draft tried in conversation; not a run of any workflow identity

text_identity.description: WR §16.3 TX-4 / CC-WR-TEXT-METHOD-ADOPTION: new App text uses chirality.app.exact-bytes.sha256/v1 over exact UTF-8 bytes. Historical and other method/value inputs remain opaque; different methods are incomparable, never relabelled.

a15_multi_descriptor.description: WR §4.7 (L-4 A as clarified): one A15 that registers several library entries in place, each entry's exact bytes bound. Offered by DEL-01-04's act control; one RS human_act with one boundSubject and boundContent per entry, in order.

reviewed_entry.description: ID-3 for a library entry: entry:<location>:<name>@<content identity>.

enum: make them available in the project library
make them available in the user library

chain_line.pattern: ^\[Chirality\] Previous workflow run ended: \S+ revision \S+ \(run \S+, (ended by the person|completed|ended to start [a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)*)\)\. Its instructions no longer apply\.$

start_line.pattern: ^\[Chirality\] Workflow run start: \S+ from the (project|user|bundled|host) library "[^"\n]+", revision \S+, run \S+\. Follow the workflow between the two markers below for this run, until the person ends the run\.$

proposal_line.description: WR section 16.2 line 3 (R20-1; RX with R20-9; RX2 with R20-11 (2)): tells the model the two agent lines and their placement; its finished line names the run's own origin and name (a reader check: it equals the run_text's workflow origin and name).
proposal_line.pattern: ^\[Chirality\] When you judge this workflow finished, end the message with a line of its own "Workflow finished: (project|user|bundled|host):(?=[a-z0-9-]{1,64}")[a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)*"\. To propose that another registered workflow runs next, end the message with a line of its own "Next workflow: <origin>:<name>", where <origin> is project, user, bundled or host; when you write both, the finished line comes just before it\. The person decides; nothing ends or starts until they confirm\.$

files_line.pattern: ^\[Chirality\] Other files of this revision, in the folder "[^"\n]+": .+$

end_line.pattern: ^\[Chirality\] Workflow run ended: \S+ revision \S+ \(run \S+, (ended by the person|completed)\)\. No workflow is in force\.$

run_text.description: WR §16 (R19-7): the text element the App composes for the turn that starts a run (purpose 'run start') or for the next turn after a run ended without a successor (purpose 'run end notice'). Framing WR-FRAME-1, PROPOSED. The record holds the lines, the identity of the workflow bytes and of the whole text; the bytes themselves stay in the revision store (linked, not copied).

ended.description: How the earlier run ended; RX2 (R20-11 (4)) adds 'ended to start <B>' for the one-step End A and start B without a finished report.

enum: agent proposal confirmed by the person

allOf.description: A chain line exactly when a chain is recorded.

supply_check.description: WR §16.6 (R19-7): one check of a run text against the turn's items as Codex returns them through thread/items/list {threadId, turnId}, all pages read (R21-4; HOSTING §4.4 'Recovery reads'). Feeds RS R3 (supplied guidance). A check is never relabelled; a later read is a new check. 'Verified' means the text was supplied as composed; whether the model followed it stays unknown (supplied is not adopted).

enum: first user message of the turn
